p-032: High-volume ingest can spend host memory bandwidth moving data that later processing discards.
Developed the STRANGLER-IPU architecture proposal and Python models comparing host pipelines with processing near the ingress boundary.
Vary input rate, useful-data fraction, and interconnect capacity to identify when early reduction could offset accelerator overhead.
Architecture research and numerical modelling. Results depend on the model assumptions; silicon, energy use, and physical interconnect performance remain unmeasured.
p-012: Remote hazard monitoring needs a way to collect sensor readings where power and connectivity are limited.
Explored a solar-powered sensor-mesh concept with ESP32 nodes and a Raspberry Pi gateway for monitoring hazards in Nepal.
The concept considered local sensing, wireless aggregation, and gateway processing as separate parts of the system.
Archived before the proposal stage. The project did not reach an implemented monitoring system; the later SPARK project became the active hardware effort.
p-007: A balancing platform needs to distinguish stable motion from conditions that require corrective action.
Developed a Random Forest stability classifier using simulated IMU data, with a FastAPI endpoint and an exported Joblib model.
Separate the sensor-feature classifier from the API so a robotics controller can consume predictions through a defined interface.
The recorded evaluation uses simulated sensor data. Its accuracy does not establish performance on physical IMU traces or prove closed-loop robot stability.
p-013: Antenna measurements stored in spreadsheets need a common representation before radiation patterns can be compared.
Prepared a Python analysis workflow that reads laboratory Excel measurements, interpolates sampled values, and produces polar plots.
Use SciPy interpolation and Matplotlib to make the measured angular response easier to inspect.
Communication and RF coursework. Interpolation fills the plotted curve between samples; it does not add new physical measurements or establish antenna calibration.
p-014: Arithmetic operations need a defined sequence of register transfers and control signals in a custom processor.
Implemented a VHDL datapath and finite-state controller for GCD and exponentiation operations as Embedded Systems coursework.
Separate datapath operations from state transitions, then inspect the resulting behaviour in Vivado simulation.
The project record documents simulation in Vivado 2023.2. It does not establish operation on an FPGA board or measured hardware timing.
p-034: Checking repository health across GitHub accounts can require repeated API requests and manual inspection of CI and commit history.
Built Python tooling for repository audits, account configuration, commit digests, and generated profile statistics.
Fetch and aggregate routine repository data locally, then pass a compact result to an assistant when interpretation is needed.
GitHub permissions, API limits, and cached data affect the result. Local aggregation avoids model calls for those operations; total token savings have not been benchmarked.
p-033: Desktop automation tied to pixel coordinates can break when a window moves or display scaling changes.
Built a Windows automation toolkit that finds controls through UI Automation and exposes operations through Python, CLI, and MCP interfaces.
Use semantic selectors for control discovery and Win32 operations for window focus, clipboard input, and screen capture.
Windows-specific tooling. Automation depends on the accessibility information an application exposes, its window state, and the permissions of the running process.
p-010: Project notes and model responses become difficult to follow when they are spread across unrelated browser sessions.
Built a React and FastAPI workspace that stores project history in SQLite and displays responses from configured model providers side by side.
Use SQLite FTS5 to retrieve project notes and attach relevant context to a request while keeping histories scoped to their project.
A local application with external model integrations. Provider credentials, model availability, and API failures still determine whether a request completes.
p-031: Notebook collections spread across accounts are difficult to search, query, and maintain from one workflow.
Built a NotebookLM dashboard and MCP server that aggregate notebook listings, support notebook queries, and manage scheduled artifact work.
Cache listings, retain account ownership, and track job state so repeated navigation and scheduling do not require another planning prompt.
Notebook access depends on authentication, sharing permissions, provider quotas, and upstream service behaviour. Cached listings can lag behind the live account state.
p-038: Scanned Nepali text and legacy Preeti encoding need different processing before they can be searched or edited as Unicode.
Built a Nepali document toolkit with OCR processing, spelling-rule checks, Preeti/Unicode conversion, and Word document repair interfaces.
Keep image recognition, character-order conversion, and text correction separate so each transformation can be inspected.
OCR depends on scan quality and the selected recognition backend. Font conversion and spelling rules do not establish document-level accuracy or guarantee correct Nepali text.
p-039: Programming problems need statements, constraints, and reference solutions in a form that can be searched and evaluated consistently.
Developed a competitive-programming archive and evaluation tooling for collecting problem material and organizing reference solutions.
Retain mathematical notation, separate statements from solutions, and use local indexing for retrieval before model-assisted analysis.
Archive coverage and solution validation vary by task. A stored solution or an exported benchmark entry does not by itself establish an accepted submission or a measured model score.
p-035: An assistant may need to move a generated file to a nearby device without using a cloud storage service.
Built an MCP server around the LocalSend protocol for LAN peer discovery and file, folder, or text transfer.
Preserve relative paths during folder transfer and expose discovery and transfer operations through explicit tool requests.
Transfers require reachable peers, compatible LocalSend clients, and recipient acceptance where required. Firewalls and network isolation can prevent discovery or delivery.
p-036: Coursework context is spread across course streams, assignments, submissions, and attached resources.
Built a Node.js MCP bridge that maps assistant tool requests to Google Classroom API operations using OAuth authentication.
Keep course and coursework identifiers explicit, refresh authorized tokens, and return structured results for downstream workflows.
Available operations depend on account permissions and API quotas. The current local course-copy checks have unresolved failures, so that path still needs repair and end-to-end verification.
p-037: A writing workflow needs to connect Markdown files, editor state, and exported documents without repeatedly locating them by hand.
Built a Windows MCP server for inspecting Typora processes, opening documents, reading recovery drafts, and managing themes and HTML exports.
Use process inspection and Typora's local files to expose document state through defined tool operations.
The integration depends on Typora's installation and local file formats. Process discovery does not guarantee that a document is saved or that every editor action can be automated.
p-002: Personal Android tools need shared navigation and settings without coupling every feature into one screen.
Built a Kotlin and Jetpack Compose application with a calculator, budget tracking, and a camera-based gesture-control module.
Keep feature screens modular and use a common application shell for state, navigation, and Android permissions.
Feature readiness varies across the application. Camera and Bluetooth behaviour require device checks; the presence of a module does not establish a published Play Store release.
p-029: Technical Markdown needs to preserve tables, code, and mathematical content when it becomes a shareable PDF.
Built a Python desktop editor, CLI, and MCP interface around shared Markdown-to-PDF conversion functions.
Select a renderer for the document's content and validate the output file. Pandoc, LaTeX, and HTML rendering paths have different formatting capabilities.
Conversion depends on installed tools and supported syntax. A successful command still needs visual review for pagination, fonts, diagrams, and layout.
p-030: Windows memory-management operations need a usable interface and clear control over when system changes run.
Built a C# and WPF utility targeting .NET 8 with memory-management operations and a background monitoring workflow.
Expose working-set and standby-list operations through Windows APIs rather than relying on a model to interpret and execute shell instructions.
Some operations require elevated permissions or undocumented Windows interfaces. Their effect depends on workload and OS behaviour; reclaimed memory is not a general performance benchmark.
p-021: A presenter needs to collect audience responses while participants and the shared display stay synchronized.
Developed a React and TypeScript polling project with choice questions, Q&A, word clouds, and QR-code joining.
Use Supabase data updates to connect voting sessions with presenter controls and the audience display.
A web application project. Concurrent attendance, reconnect behaviour, and response latency need a live session test; no capacity claim is made from the archived preview.
p-020: Alphametic puzzles require distinct digits for letters while satisfying carries, arithmetic, and leading-zero constraints.
Built a column-by-column backtracking solver, an answer checker, and a FastAPI wrapper for puzzle requests and optional metrics.
Reject assignments as soon as a column violates the arithmetic constraints rather than enumerating every complete mapping.
The solver handles the supported addition-puzzle format. Search cost depends on the puzzle; the recorded examples do not establish a fixed solve-time guarantee.
p-015: First-time React learners need small examples whose state changes they can trace while following a workshop.
Prepared a Vite-based teaching application for the IEEE KEC workshop, progressing from greeting and props examples to counters and a live clock.
Keep each lesson in a separate component so learners can connect a change in code with its effect in the browser.
Instructional material for an introductory workshop. The application demonstrates React concepts; it does not include the operational requirements of a deployed product.
p-003: A model cannot support useful analysis until missing values, feature relationships, and class balance are understood.
Prepared a data-wrangling notebook for a synthetic heart-attack-risk dataset as Fuse AI Fellowship coursework.
Inspect distributions, correlations, and class imbalance before preparing the data for downstream modelling.
An exploratory analysis of synthetic data. The notebook does not establish clinical risk prediction, patient safety, or applicability to real hospital records.
p-004: Customer, order, and payment records need consistent validation and persistence across API requests.
Built a FastAPI application with SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL, including record-management endpoints and a statistics module.
Separate database access from request handling and use environment-based configuration, container setup, and centralized logging.
A fellowship API implementation. Deployment configuration alone does not establish production availability, access-control completeness, or performance under concurrent traffic.
p-005: A natural-language database question needs to become valid SQL before its result can be explained to a user.
Built a PostgreSQL-backed pipeline that plans a query, generates SQL, validates it, executes it, and summarizes the result.
Separate query generation from validation and execution, then compare outputs against the assignment's reference questions and SQL.
Evaluation is bounded by the coursework schema and recorded question set. Successful queries there do not establish correctness on unfamiliar schemas or authorization to execute arbitrary SQL.
p-006: Customer retention work combines a binary churn decision with an estimate of customer lifetime value.
Built classification and regression workflows using linear-model families, with diagnostic plots and an exported notebook report.
Compare model behaviour across the churn and value-prediction tasks rather than using one score for both objectives.
An offline coursework analysis. Results depend on the dataset, target definitions, and evaluation split; they do not demonstrate an intervention that reduces churn.
p-008: Churn classification must account for class imbalance without allowing resampling to leak into validation data.
Built a Telco churn pipeline using tree-based ensembles, with a separate tenure-regression task and model documentation.
Restrict SMOTE to training folds and inspect feature contributions with SHAP alongside the model comparison.
Offline fellowship coursework. Explanations describe the fitted model's behaviour on the evaluated data; they do not establish causal drivers of customer churn.
p-009: A point estimate can hide uncertainty that matters when comparing predictions or updating beliefs from new observations.
Implemented probabilistic-modelling exercises covering MLE, MAP estimation, Bayesian updating, graphical models, and PyMC logistic regression.
Retain posterior samples and use ArviZ diagnostics to inspect the fitted Bayesian model rather than reporting only a single coefficient estimate.
Coursework examples under explicit model and prior assumptions. Sampling diagnostics assess the fitted inference run; they do not prove that those assumptions match a deployment population.
p-011: Retail transaction data has no predefined customer segments, so the feature representation shapes the groups a clustering method finds.
Built an Online Retail II segmentation workflow with RFM and category-ratio features, then compared K-Means, hierarchical clustering, and DBSCAN.
Inspect cluster structure with silhouette and Davies-Bouldin scores and relate the groups back to their transaction features.
An exploratory segmentation exercise. Internal clustering scores do not establish durable customer categories or measured campaign value.
p-016: Time-series models must be compared on future observations without leaking information from later periods into training.
Built a forecasting notebook comparing classical and machine-learning models, an ensemble, and forecast diagnostics.
Evaluate errors with MASE and RMSE and examine whether combining forecasts changes the comparison with individual models.
The recorded environment could not fetch Yahoo Finance data and used a seeded synthetic fallback. Those results demonstrate the pipeline, not predictive performance on the real S&P 500.
p-017: Steel surface-defect classification needs a model that learns image structure while exposing overfitting on the available dataset.
Built a PyTorch CNN workflow for the six NEU defect classes, with augmentation, normalization, and dropout experiments.
Compare training and validation behaviour while tuning the model, rather than treating training accuracy as evidence of generalization.
An offline image-classification assignment. The evaluation does not establish detection performance on a production line, unseen cameras, or a different defect distribution.
p-019: Fruit images need to be separated into usable regions before shapes and object locations can be inspected.
Built an OpenCV workflow for HSV segmentation, morphological cleanup, denoising, and edge and feature detection.
Implement the Canny stages directly, compare them with OpenCV, and inspect how detection changes when fruit touches or image noise increases.
Classical image-processing coursework on the selected image sets. Thresholds and geometric assumptions need retuning for different lighting, backgrounds, and camera conditions.
p-022: Classification, object detection, and segmentation answer different visual questions and need separate evaluation criteria.
Built a computer-vision coursework notebook covering ResNet transfer learning, Faster R-CNN, DeepLab segmentation, a VAE, and transformer-based image representations.
Compare learned and zero-shot representations, inspect GradCAM outputs, and consider export requirements in the assignment's deployment scenario.
Notebook experiments on selected datasets and image slices. The warehouse-camera rollout is a coursework scenario; the project does not establish operation across a deployed camera fleet.
p-024: Text-routing workflows need entity boundaries and types before names and locations can be used as structured fields.
Built a CoNLL-2003 named-entity workflow with preprocessing, token features, a CRF model, and error analysis.
Combine word-shape and neighbouring-token features, then inspect entity-level precision and recall alongside individual mistakes.
The source dataset is general-domain annotated text. The customer-support framing is an assignment scenario; transfer to real tickets and CRM data requires separate evaluation.
p-027: A text classifier needs to map variable-length headlines into a fixed set of topic labels.
Implemented an AG_NEWS headline classifier with a constructed vocabulary, an embedding layer, an LSTM, and a final classification layer.
Build the PyTorch training and inference flow from the supplied notebook skeleton and inspect the effect of sequence representation on predictions.
A four-topic coursework classifier with recorded notebook outputs. Performance on the assignment data does not establish robustness to new topics, languages, or changing news vocabulary.
p-028: A support message must reach the correct handling category before a specialized assistant can respond.
Developed encoder and decoder-model routing approaches for eleven customer-support categories using the Bitext dataset.
Use a group-aware stratified split to keep repeated instruction text from crossing training and evaluation boundaries, then compare the candidate routing approaches.
An intent-classification experiment. Routing labels measure category selection; they do not establish the correctness of a downstream agent's answer or its business action.
p-045: An assistant needs retrieved context and bounded tool use when a model response alone is insufficient.
Built a FastAPI assistant with Qdrant retrieval, structured responses, tool calling, and a Streamlit interface.
Use caching, retries, circuit breakers, and a provider fallback chain to handle repeated requests and unavailable model services.

A fellowship implementation. Retrieval quality and response correctness depend on the corpus and provider; configured fallbacks do not guarantee that an unavailable service will be replaced successfully.
p-046: A single retrieval pass can miss information, follow outdated context, or produce citations that were never retrieved.
Extended the RAG assistant with an iterative tool-use loop, context management, and a deterministic citation-verification gate.
Clear old tool results while retaining notes, cap the loop's budget, and record trajectories and failures in a custom evaluation harness.
The saved report covers four cases and includes a provider failure. Citation checks establish source membership, not the factual correctness of every answer.
p-044: An assistant can receive sensitive inputs and return malformed, unsupported, or sensitive outputs.
Built a guardrail pipeline with input checks for PII and prompt injection, plus output checks for schema conformity, groundedness, and leakage.
Keep checks around the generation step and use a curated evaluation set to inspect which cases are blocked, accepted, or require fallback handling.
Checks cover the implemented rules and recorded cases. They do not establish complete jailbreak resistance, comprehensive PII detection, or guaranteed factual correctness.
p-026: An organizational case study needs evidence about how responsibilities and hiring practices work beyond a company's public description.
Prepared an Organization and Management coursework study of Fusemachines, drawing on an interview with Talent Acquisition and PR managers.
Connect the interview material to organizational structure, HR practices, and cross-functional operations in a written report with LaTeX sources.
An academic case study based on the available interview and documentation. It represents that study's scope and period, rather than an ongoing audit of the company.
